title: Build CLI expense tracker: add, list, total commands
objective: Deliver a working command-line expense tracker so a single user can record expenses and see a running total, with data persisted between runs.
current_state: Empty repository. No source files, no tests, no packaging metadata exist yet.
target_behavior: Running `expense add <amount> <category> [--note TEXT]` appends a persisted record and exits 0. Running `expense list [--category TEXT]` prints all recorded expenses newest-first, one per line. Running `expense total [--category TEXT]` prints the sum of matching amounts formatted to exactly two decimal places.
input_format: CLI arguments via argparse: `add AMOUNT CATEGORY [--note TEXT]`, `list [--category TEXT]`, `total [--category TEXT]`. AMOUNT is a decimal string, e.g. '12.50'.
output_format: Plain text to stdout. `list` prints one line per record as 'DATE  AMOUNT  CATEGORY  NOTE', newest first. `total` prints a single line: the decimal sum formatted to two places.
error_handling: A non-numeric or unparsable AMOUNT must print an error to stderr and exit with code 1, without writing a record.
A negative AMOUNT must be rejected with an error message and exit code 1.
If the data file is missing, create a new empty one instead of failing.
If the data file exists but contains a corrupted line, skip that line, continue processing the rest, and print a warning to stderr.
completion_criteria: `expense add 12.50 food --note lunch` appends a record to the data file and exits 0.
`expense list` prints all recorded expenses newest-first, including the one just added.
`expense total` prints the correct decimal sum of all recorded amounts, formatted to two decimal places.
manual_verification: Run `python -m expense_tracker add 12.50 food --note lunch` then `python -m expense_tracker list` and confirm the new entry appears at the top.
Run `python -m expense_tracker add -5 food` and confirm it is rejected with a non-zero exit code.

delegation.justification: This task is an independently verifiable bounded outcome with its own contract scope.
